phase_name: Probe completion — manifest drift, duplicate blocks, ranked ordering

objectives.description: Add manifest_registered via check-extension-docs.sh Rule Q invocation
Add duplicated-block detection across scripts (bounded fixed-window hashing)
Add stable ranked ordering with documented composite score
Add --check mode exit semantics for zero-caller/manifest-drift findings
Extend test suite for new metrics

approaches_tried.approach: Weight duplicate_blocks at x20 in the composite score
approaches_tried.reason: On the real corpus this let a 1,635-line script with 172 duplicate-window hits (score 5075) outrank the corpus's actual largest script, orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (3,026 lines, score 3026) -- violating the plan's own Phase 2 verification criterion that ranking[0] must be orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh. Reduced duplicate_blocks weight to x1 (a low-weight modifier, not a competing primary signal) and re-verified: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh ranks #1 with the real weight applied, and the gap to the runner-up (claude-refresh.sh, 2445 lines) is far larger than any realistic modifier contribution.

approaches_tried.approach: Build fixture-only check-extension-docs.sh Rule Q tests inside a plain mktemp -d (non-git) directory
approaches_tried.reason: check_undeclared_scripts uses `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files`, which errors out silently on a non-git directory, so Rule Q never fires and every candidate reports manifest_registered=true regardless of real registration status. Fixed by using git-initialized fixtures (git init + add + commit) for every manifest_registered test case, matching the no-side-effects suite's own git-fixture convention.
